role: Classify and explain final acceptability of the untouched draft. Never rewrite, approve, or promote it.
compactRubric: Read-aloud rule: does every central sentence sound natural and literal when spoken?
Morning-reader test: do the early sentences stay short, carry one idea each, and make sense on one tired read without reparsing?
Does the draft name a recognizable pressure, action, and consequence?
Is the subject matter supported by the verified astrology?
Does the draft follow the applicable surface contract?
Does it resemble the owner passages rather than generic astrology, institutional prose, therapy copy, corporate advice, or a polished slogan?
Would any central sentence need to be translated into ordinary English?

decisions.rule: Use ordinary, current language that makes literal sense when read aloud.
decisions.rationale: The owner repeatedly rejected polished wording that no one would normally say.
examplesAllowed: Everyone else has to change their plans later.
examplesRejected: The banished want refuses to stay reasonable.
The arrangement stopped telling the truth.

decisions.rule: Name the pressure, what someone does, and what changes because of it in one recognizable sequence.
decisions.rationale: Concrete nouns alone do not create authored writing; the sequence needs pressure, choice, and consequence.
examplesAllowed: Saying yes avoids the discomfort of saying no, then everyone else has to change their plans later.
examplesRejected: A family member stops being the automatic host; a workplace questions the arrangement.

decisions.rule: Calendar Sky aspect copy never uses you, your, yours, yourself, or yourselves; Sky placement copy may address the reader directly.
decisions.rationale: Calendar Sky aspects describe collective events, while Sky placement pages may speak directly to the reader under the owner-approved page register.
examplesAllowed: The aspect changes what the group can agree to.

decisions.rule: People is allowed in Sky Placement copy, used sparingly. Overuse is a semantic review signal, not a deterministic failure. On other surfaces, use it only when the collective itself is the real subject.
decisions.rationale: Owner ruling 2026-08-11, applied to this branch 2026-08-14. Sky Placement is collective copy and people belongs there in moderation. Concealing an available specific subject remains a review matter, judged in the cold read rather than by regex.
examplesAllowed: A sibling stops hosting every holiday.
examplesRejected: People can care deeply and still leave the rule untouched.

decisions.rule: Person is allowed. Prohibit repetitive generic phrases such as one person when a more specific role, action, or subject is available.
decisions.rationale: The word is natural in owner writing; repetition becomes formulaic and can hide who acts.
examplesAllowed: The person who remembers every birthday keeps the spare key.
examplesRejected: One person decides. One person explains. One person fixes it.

decisions.rule: Looks good on paper is allowed as an ordinary idiom. Other uses of on paper require an actual written document; administrative put the plan on paper phrasing is prohibited.
decisions.rationale: The owner uses the ordinary idiom but rejected AI-generated administrative instructions.
examplesAllowed: It looks good on paper.
The signed contract exists on paper.
examplesRejected: Put the emergency plan on paper.

decisions.rule: Room is allowed for a literal physical room. Prohibit stock audience or hierarchy phrases such as the loudest person in the room or the smartest voice in the room.
decisions.rationale: Literal rooms provide useful evidence; room-as-audience phrasing is a stock hierarchy cliché.
examplesAllowed: A guest room turns into an office.
examplesRejected: The loudest person in the room becomes the plan.
The smartest voice in the room takes over.

decisions.rule: Reserve harm and self-harm for literal harm. Do not substitute self-harm for broader language; otherwise name the specific behavior, loss, danger, or consequence.
decisions.rationale: Severity should match what actually happened, and the older automatic replacement made ordinary consequences sound harsher than intended.
examplesAllowed: The fall caused physical harm.

decisions.rule: Steady is allowed for observable effort, pace, support, light, or reliability. Prohibit it only as vague energy language or an empty positive adjective.
decisions.rationale: Published owner writing uses steady naturally; the earlier stable, strong, or solid qualifier rule did not evaluate the noun or sentence.
examplesAllowed: A full day in Taurus emphasizes steady effort.
The support remains steady.

decisions.rule: Perform, performed, and performance are allowed only for literal acting, music, presentations, or measurable job performance. Prohibit figurative uses about identity, normalcy, worth, emotion, belonging, or social behavior; Leo alone is not an exception.
decisions.rationale: The words are ordinary in literal performance contexts but repeatedly became polished figurative framing in generated copy.
examplesAllowed: The actor prepares for the performance.
The manager reviews quarterly job performance.
examplesRejected: Life is not a performance review.

literal_exceptions: an actual physical object is tilted

decisions.rule: Do not use tilt or tilts as a figurative substitute for change. Literal physical tilting is allowed.
decisions.rationale: The owner rejected tilt in this phrasing and explicitly retained the physical-object exception.
examplesAllowed: The table tilts toward the window.
examplesRejected: A dinner plan starts to tilt.

decisions.rule: A tagline must be a clear full sentence readers understand on first read. Strong is welcome; cryptic compression is not.
decisions.rationale: The owner retired Stop calling silence peace because the compressed line did not make sense without explanation.
examplesAllowed: The disagreement starts before the cancellation.

decisions.rule: When the behavior and cost are clear, stop; delete a following slogan, metaphor, reassurance, or second conclusion.
decisions.rationale: Stacked endings repeatedly turn a strong paragraph into polished generated copy.
examplesAllowed: After enough of this, no one trusts what is said anymore.
examplesRejected: That is the lesson. That is the opening. That is where the future begins.

decisions.rule: Do not turn ordinary events into institutional, advocacy, therapy-workbook, or corporate-operations language unless the actual subject requires it.
decisions.rationale: These registers repeatedly replace recognizable behavior with categories and reports.
examplesAllowed: Everyone else has to change their plans later.
examplesRejected: Document the task and record what fails.

literal_exceptions: physical mail is part of the source or scene

decisions.rule: Use message, reply, response, or what they were told instead of letter or formal technical delivery terms unless physical mail matters.
decisions.rationale: Letter sounded dated, while portal notification and electronic correspondence sounded technical rather than current.
examplesAllowed: Three families compare the messages they received.
A handwritten letter arrives in the mail.
examplesRejected: Three families receive the same portal notification.

decisions.rule: Flag sentences matching the documented CC/SD constructions in voice/banned-constructions.json because they read as CC or SD rather than the house voice. Owner-verbatim text is exempt. Treat this as a judged consideration, not an automatic score failure; falsifiable language versus unsupported affirmation is the tiebreaker.
decisions.rationale: Generated astrology copy drifts toward the genre's two dominant sites by default, while a small number of house-approved moves sit near the boundary.
examplesAllowed: Owner-verbatim text is exempt.

decisions.rule: Chani-adjacent warmth, tenderness, permission, emotional intelligence, and moderate lyrical cadence are allowed. Documented adjacent-site constructions and advocacy-default subject matter are not.
decisions.rationale: Softness is not the problem; recognizable borrowed constructions and the wrong recurring subject matter are.
examplesAllowed: Warm, emotionally observant permission to do one nameable thing.
examplesRejected: Let's dive into what the stars have in store.

decisions.rule: Collective astrology does not default to campaigns, institutions, policy, organizing, public harm, or collective healing. Those subjects require direct astrological and owner-source support.
decisions.rationale: Collective was repeatedly translated into generic progressive-publication subject matter rather than Marie's recurring concerns.
examplesAllowed: A platform changes who gets heard.
examplesRejected: The denial becomes evidence and turns into a public campaign.

decisions.rule: Do not infer a life domain from a sign alone. Taurus does not automatically mean work or career.
decisions.rationale: A planet, house, aspect, or verified source must support the chosen domain.
examplesAllowed: Work appears when the supplied astrology supports employment.
examplesRejected: Taurus makes this transit about work.

decisions.rule: Reject the swappable tagline construction [Planet] in [sign] helps us grow through [generic virtue or domain]. A tagline must tell the reader what is actually happening.
decisions.rationale: Naming a placement and generic virtue produces interchangeable astrology copy rather than a recognizable line.
examplesAllowed: The plan changes when someone finally says what they want.
examplesRejected: Jupiter in Libra helps us grow through fair, honest partnership.

decisions.rule: Reject the stock gift-to-problem keyword flip: The gift becomes the problem when [positive keyword] turns into [negative keyword]. Show the observed sequence instead.
decisions.rationale: The formula reads like a generic astrology gift-and-shadow template.
examplesAllowed: The cancellation is where the disagreement finally shows up.
examplesRejected: The gift becomes the problem when diplomacy turns into avoidance.

decisions.rule: For ordinary shared decisions, reject workshop, mediation, negotiation, and facilitation language unless the literal subject requires it. Name what someone wants, avoids saying, delays, and causes instead.
decisions.rationale: The controlled draft converted a dinner plan into a facilitated compromise exercise.
examplesAllowed: Someone says no before everyone else changes their plans later.
examplesRejected: shape an answer each side can support

decisions.rule: Do not build a Sky Placement article around a low-stakes social plan merely because a sign suggests partnership. A social plan must expose a recognizable pressure with a meaningful consequence and cannot stage a perfectly balanced solution to prove the astrology.
decisions.rationale: The dinner-and-live-music solution was manufactured to demonstrate compromise rather than reveal a consequential pattern.
examplesAllowed: A social plan whose delayed refusal changes trust or creates a real cost.
examplesRejected: A perfectly accommodated dinner plan with no meaningful stakes.

decisions.rule: Reject generic fairness conclusions that explain a virtue instead of ending on the specific behavior and cost established by the article.
decisions.rationale: The controlled article ended with a universal principle that could close many unrelated relationship articles.
examplesAllowed: After enough of this, no one trusts what is said anymore.
examplesRejected: Fairness requires each side to be heard before the choice is made.

decisions.rule: A central register failure spanning hook, lived section, turn, and moves is a full-draft rejection. Do not reduce it to one weak tagline or one isolated sentence.
decisions.rationale: Terra rated the controlled Jupiter-in-Libra draft borderline and named only the tagline despite formal negotiation language and workshop framing throughout.
examplesRejected: The complete controlled Jupiter-in-Libra v3 Sol draft.

decisions.rule: Reject sign-cliche stock scenes when they govern the central opening, tension, and development sequence. Isolated practical moves are exempt unless the central scene itself is a scheduling or dinner scene. The scene must follow from this placement's combined meaning at this transit's scale, and a year-long or slower transit cannot be reduced to one evening's logistics.
decisions.rationale: The rejected Jupiter-in-Libra draft passed the earlier checks while reproducing the named Libra dinner-plan meme and shrinking a year-long transit to one evening.
examplesAllowed: A sequence whose pressure and consequence could only follow from the combined planet and sign meaning at the stated duration.
A creative-collaboration article may include separate moves about answering an invitation and naming which day works; those moves do not turn the central scene into invitation scheduling.
examplesRejected: Libra friends cannot choose a restaurant or dinner plan.
Aries goes to the gym or gets an impulsive haircut.
Cancer takes a bubble bath or cancels plans.

decisions.rule: Moves must sound like actions someone would actually say they took, not workshop, facilitation, negotiation, or project-management instructions. Until an exact owner-approved moves exemplar exists, the moves section is the highest-risk section and any listed facilitation term there is a score-1 failure.
decisions.rationale: The owner corpus does not yet supply an approved bulleted-moves exemplar, and the rejected draft invented facilitation-workshop language.
examplesAllowed: An ordinary action stated in words someone would use after doing it.

decisions.rule: Apply an owner-register check even when every deterministic rule passes. Generic product copy fails. Compare only against eligible owner evidence, and cite the three weakest lines. Never treat an unapproved card as a format exemplar.
decisions.rationale: Terra passed a mechanically clean draft that the owner rejected as generic product copy.
examplesAllowed: A draft whose observations and sentence movement are plausibly the owner's.
examplesRejected: Jupiter in Libra helps us grow through fair, honest partnership.

decisions.rule: A qualitative, non-numeric subperiod may trace to a reviewed residency fact only when it cannot exceed that residency. Numeric or date-like subperiods still require an explicit engine fact or render token.
decisions.rationale: Narrative pacing inside a known residency window is not a new moving fact, but numeric and calendar-like claims must remain engine-owned.
examplesAllowed: A few months in
Early in the transit
By midyear

decisions.rule: Apply the morning-reader test: every sentence must make sense on one tired read, with short sentences early, one idea per opening sentence, and no construction that requires a second pass to parse.
decisions.rationale: Readers often open these write-ups first thing in the morning while they are still waking up.
examplesAllowed: The answer changed. We ask what changed with it.
examplesRejected: A long opening sentence that combines the scene, interpretation, astrology, timing, and conclusion before the reader can find the point.

decisions.rule: Do not use leak, leaks, leaked, or leaking in Marie Satori editorial copy. Name the observable action or consequence instead.
decisions.rationale: The house style guide already prohibited leak language for emotion or expression, and the owner confirmed that leak is an AI tell she does not use.
examplesAllowed: After enough of this, no one trusts what is said anymore.
examplesRejected: Say the raw thing and it clears. Hold it in and it leaks out sideways, aimed at whoever is closest.

decisions.rule: The complete controlled Jupiter-in-Libra v3 Sol draft is owner-rejected and may serve only as negative evaluation evidence.
decisions.rationale: The owner rejected the writing as a whole, not only Terra's weakest-line diagnosis.
examplesRejected: The complete controlled Jupiter-in-Libra v3 Sol draft.

decisions.rule: Keep the architecture fixed: verified astrology supplies meaning, Sol writes one draft, deterministic checks catch hard failures, Terra judges afterward, and only the owner approves exact wording.
decisions.rationale: Durable corrections should update scoped policy and regression tests rather than trigger another architecture redesign.

decisions.rule: Only the owner may approve exact wording. Better, good, great, preferred wording, and judge scores do not grant exact approval or promotion.
decisions.rationale: Writing, judging, exact approval, calibration use, generation evidence, and production promotion are separate permissions.

decisions.rule: Display time in the user's local timezone; computed dates, degrees, motion, and event times come from the engine rather than generated prose.
decisions.rationale: Reader output must not hardcode PT or hand-write moving facts.
examplesRejected: All event times are shown in PT.

decisions.rule: Use 17 arcminutes as the primary traditional cazimi figure; a claim of within 1 degree must be flaggable.
decisions.rationale: The reference fact bank distinguishes the primary traditional figure from broader modern usage.
examplesAllowed: Cazimi is within 17 arcminutes under the primary traditional figure.

decisions.rule: The Barbault quote remains unverified and cannot serve until independently confirmed.
decisions.rationale: Unverified quotations cannot become factual authority.

decisions.rule: Uranus in Cancer v3 is exact owner-approved calibration evidence only.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly limited approval to judge calibration.

prohibitedActions: treat calibration-only approval as writer evidence
